auth.label: Login, recuperação de senha e limites

rules.rule: Tenant-scoped operations run through the tenant helpers (withTenant, withSalon, withUser, withSalonBySlug, withInviteToken).
Tenant, role and ownership are validated on the server; hiding a UI element does not authorize anything.
rules.source: AGENTS.md > Regras não negociáveis; DECISOES_PRODUTO.md > matriz de papéis

rules.rule: Row Level Security is enabled and forced on the tenant tables.
The application runtime connects as app_runtime, a role without BYPASSRLS, never as postgres.
Tenant policies are based on app_current_salon().
A record cannot reference a record of another tenant: tenant relations use composite constraints with the salon id.
Reserving products for an appointment fails when the appointment or a product belongs to another salon.
Cancellations, suspensions and billing never delete history.
A professional sees only their own agenda.
A professional sees only the clients linked to their own appointments.
A professional has no access to financial data.
Reception has no access to reports, expenses or commissions.
At checkout, reception can only record the payment method received.
A client sees only their own appointments.
Only the owner and the manager can use the scheduling override.
An override requires confirmation and a reason, and is recorded immutably with the person responsible.
An override never bypasses tenant, authentication, data integrity or status transitions.
The global administration area (/plataforma) is reachable only by PlatformRole.SUPER_ADMIN.
A team invitation token is random with 256 bits.
Only the SHA-256 of the invitation token is persisted.
A team invitation is valid for 24 hours.
Resending an invitation rotates its token.
An invitation is consumed once, atomically, in PostgreSQL.
Accepting an invitation with an existing account requires the recipient's session.
A new account is activated only after a valid invitation flow.
An invitation never changes the password of an existing account.
An owner or manager of another salon cannot reset the password or attach the account of someone else.
There is at most one pending invitation per salon and normalized email.
While email delivery is off, every invitation operation fails closed and no manual fallback link exists.
Public booking ignores any clientId sent by the browser.
An authenticated client is identified only by the signed session and the salon present in that session.
A visitor creates an isolated contact: a phone or email cannot be used to take over an existing client profile.
Client history and cancellation require a session and cross the client id with the salon id.
The password recovery token is consumed only when the new password is submitted, not when the link is opened, which protects against email scanners.
Password recovery requests always return a generic answer, including provider-specific account errors.
The recovery rate limit by IP does not depend on whether the email exists.
Admin login, client login and invitation use separate rate-limit buckets.
Authentication and sensitive writes fail closed when the rate limiter (Redis) is missing or unavailable.
In production the trusted client IP comes only from x-vercel-forwarded-for.
The cron endpoint answers 401 when CRON_SECRET is missing, empty or wrong.
Passwords, hashes, tokens, cookies and secrets are never logged.
An account linked to the official provider is granted access by the provider user UUID, not by an editable email or metadata.
An upload requires a session, an allowed role and a membership in the active salon.
An upload never accepts a user-supplied path; files are stored under salonId/purpose/uuid.ext.
An upload checks the MIME type and the magic bytes and rejects SVG.
